answer: A work-backed reputation thread makes fake identities expensive: each agent must accumulate a verifiable history of useful, attested work before it can transact at full trust. A new account starts hollow, with no history and tight limits, so spinning up thousands of copies buys nothing by itself. Building trust requires sustained, checkable contributions over time, like a quill that only gains authority after many signed entries. An attacker must pay the full time and compute cost for every identity, while honest agents keep their earned standing, so Sybil floods collapse under their own cost.
